sphere_commentary.overview:
The data set validates the Drum Protocols architecture across three series with consistent efficacy patterns.
• HEALING leads in sample size (n=574) with highest mean (6.98) and lowest variance (std=1.77), confirming strong nervous system regulation
• THRIVING achieves comparable mean (6.96) with particularly strong Focus & Clarity outcomes (T-FC-L3 mean=7.63)
• TRANSFORMING shows widest spread (std=1.87) consistent with ascending-arc design complexity
• 1,000 outcome scores provide strong signal; 614 contextual responses enable meaningful qualitative triangulation
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
Series efficacy aligns with design intent, but with notable variation in reach.
• HEALING: DESCENT protocols excel (mean 7.0+), with over-stimulation and sleep zones strongest; crisis protocols show expected lower baseline
• THRIVING: HOLD protocols show upward trajectory in higher levels; Focus & Clarity outliers (L3) merit investigation for cross-series learnings
• TRANSFORMING: ASCENT protocols carry widest variance; X-MD-L3 emerges as unexpected high performer in motivation zone despite low n
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several protocols show divergence between observed outcomes and AutoGluon predictions warranting investigation.
• X-ME-L1: Model predicts highest efficacy (score=8.23) across five zones despite moderate observed mean (6.74) — largest prediction gap in dataset
• X-MC-L3: Lowest mean (5.7) with highest std (2.45), strongest candidate for bimodality in TRANSFORMING series
• H-SL-L1/H-SL-L2: Extreme embedding drift (sim=0.530, 0.681) suggests analytical instability rather than protocol shift
• T-FC-L3: Outlier high performer (mean=7.63, 71% positive) with notably higher YouTube visibility (views=15)
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
AutoGluon cross-bucket routing and embedding drift flags specific protocols for targeted action.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-ME-L1: Test broader deployment — model predicts strong efficacy across anxiety, crisis, low-affect, focus, and maintenance zones
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-MC-L3: Create new L2 variant with more gradual descent — current L3 shows 5.7 mean with 2.45 std, potential ceiling or entry-point issue
• X-MD-L3: Investigate outlier performance (mean=7.15 from n=13) — highest drift (sim=0.507) indicates either analytical shift or genuine efficacy signal
• T-FC-L3: Analyze L3 configuration for cross-series transfer — highest THRIVING performer (mean=7.63) with strong positive rate (71%)
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
High cross-run drift across protocols indicates analytical evolution or unstable signal interpretation.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: 25 of 30 protocols show cosine similarity < 0.85 — unusually high instability likely reflects model recalibration rather than true data shift
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: T-FC-L1↔T-FC-L2 (sim=0.878), H-SL-L1↔H-SL-L2 (sim=0.869) confirm analytically coherent protocol families; H-OS-L3 (mean_sim=0.677) is most distinct protocol
• Confidence note: Drift based on 8 prior runs — sufficient quantity but may reflect narrative adaptation rather than protocol efficacy change

by_protocol.X-MD-L2: n=14, mean=6.21, std=1.63, confidence=developing. Slightly lower than L1. Settle times slow (5 at 20 min, 5 at 10 min). 9/21 'loved it' on music suggests subjective quality despite low mean. High drift (sim=0.585). AutoGluon cross-bucket suggests X-ME-L1 as alternative.
by_protocol.X-MD-L3: n=13, mean=7.15, std=2.38, confidence=developing. Highest mean in motivation series despite smallest n. 62% positive — strong recovery signal. Extreme drift (sim=0.507) — most unstable protocol in dataset. Small n limits confidence but divergence from L1/L2 pattern warrants deep investigation of this variant.
by_protocol.X-ME-L1: n=39, mean=6.74, std=1.94, confidence=meaningful. Mood ASCENT shows moderate outcome but AutoGluon predicts 8.230 across five zones (anxiety, crisis, low, focus, maintenance) — strongest cross-bucket signal in analysis. Qualitative: 10/22 'loved it' on music. High drift (sim=0.818). Views=8. The gap between observed and predicted is largest in dataset — investigate routing or reach barriers.
by_protocol.X-ME-L2: n=25, mean=6.76, std=1.71, confidence=meaningful. Slightly higher than L1. 6/15 'loved it' music. Fast settling pattern (4 immediate, 4 at 20 min). High drift (sim=0.532). Views=8. AutoGluon predicts across zones — similar potential to L1 but less pronounced gap.
by_protocol.X-ME-L3: n=18, mean=6.28, std=1.74, confidence=developing. Lowest in mood series. 5/22 'no effect' — notable for ASCENT. Drift moderate (sim=0.627). Views=4 lowest in series. Mixed rhythm feedback suggests groovestyle sensitivity. Small n and low reach limit interpretation.

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: This is one of the most effective anxiety protocols — most people feel noticeably better, typically settling within 5-10 minutes. The steady rhythm feels calming to listeners.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: Helps with stress and anxiety, with outcomes similar to the L1 version. Some find the music style takes getting used to, but most report improvement.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: A good option for anxiety that works especially well for those who need deeper calming — settle times tend toward 10 minutes, and the rhythm is described as very settling.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Designed for high-distress moments, this protocol shows significant improvement for about a third of users. Results vary based on how acute the distress is when starting.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: Provides support during crisis moments for some, though less consistent than other crisis protocols. The rhythm feels settling to about half of listeners.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: Works quickly for certain users in crisis — several people settled within minutes. However, not everyone finds it effective, suggesting it works best for specific situations.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: One of the top performers across all protocols — helps most listeners calm from overstimulation. People really like the sound and notice improvement within about 10 minutes.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Effective for sensory overwhelm, though the music style divides opinions. Most who respond well settle within 10 minutes.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Works well for overstimulation and interestingly also shows up in sleep-related contexts. Some find the rhythm calming, though a few find it too active.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: A top sleep protocol — most listeners settle quickly (around 5 minutes), with many falling asleep. The music is well-liked and the rhythm feels steady.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: Works for sleep and relaxation, though slightly less consistent than L1. Used frequently by caregivers supporting others — some find the rhythm a bit too active.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: Helps many relax and rest, though some didn't fully settle during the session. Notably used in caregiving situations for supporting others.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: Gives a gentle boost in creative focus — results are mild and gradual, with some people feeling slight improvement over time.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: Slightly more effective than L1 for creativity, with many loving the music style. Settling takes longer, around 10 minutes.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: Shows the strongest creative flow results in its series — helps more people tap into creativity, though results still vary by individual.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: A foundational focus protocol that helps some but shows room for improvement. Some find the rhythm slightly distracting.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: Works better than L1 for focus, with notable improvement especially in therapy and caregiving settings. Music opinions are mixed.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: The standout focus protocol — the most effective in the THRIVING series, with 71% reporting positive change and many describing significant improvement.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: Supports maintenance and balance with consistent outcomes. Takes longer to effect (20+ minutes) for some listeners.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: More variable than its sibling — some find it helpful, others don't connect with it. The rhythm divides opinions.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: Helps maintain balance for most, though a small group didn't settle at all. More research needed given smaller sample size.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: Guides to calmer thinking — most people feel better but a rare few (2 out of 25) felt slightly worse, an important signal to track.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: Most find it helps clear the mind, with many describing the rhythm as very settling. Fast-acting for some.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: Shows the weakest results in this series, with the widest variance. Some feel clearer, others don't notice much — may need parameter adjustment.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: Targets motivation from lower energy states. About 45% feel positive change, others less so — baseline matters significantly here.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: Helps some find motivation but takes time (often 20 minutes). Music is loved by some despite modest overall outcomes.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: Surprisingly strong for motivation despite small sample — many report moderate improvement. Notably different from earlier versions in this series.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: A gentle mood lifter with interesting cross-category potential — the data suggests it could work well beyond its designed zone. Loved by many for its music.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: Similar to L1 but with faster action for some. Strong positive reception from those who connect with the music style.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: More variable results than siblings — some feel a lift, others don't. Works quietly in background for daily activities.
